title: Failover sim scripts, circuit-breaker tuning, and rollback verification
creator: Liam Patel
description: Objective: Build and validate a reusable simulation framework for active-passive failover that exercises circuit breakers, load-shedding policies, and backup/restore verification. The framework should produce actionable telemetry (SLO breaches, error budgets consumed, and per-region latency/capacity signals) and a set of canonical failure scenarios used in quarterly drills. Scope excludes orchestration UI changes; the work focuses on simulation scripts, verification checks, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation framework can trigger a controlled passive-region blackout and measure failover latency and error rates
Circuit breaker triggers and recovery behavior are observable and parameterizable via config
Load-shedding policy test cases validate graceful degradation without SLO violation beyond allowed error budget thresholds
Automated backup restore verification runs against the latest daily snapshot and reports checksums + row counts
A dry-run drill can be completed in staging within 90 minutes with a post-mortem template auto-populated
steps: Create a small Python-based runner that dispatches traffic patterns against the load balancer and can mute a target region by simulating network blackhole or shutting the router group
Implement hooks to flip circuit breaker states (trip/untrip) and measure downstream queue growth and 5xx spikes
Add synthetic load-shedding client that opens lower-priority request paths and asserts 429 vs 503 behavior under load
Integrate backup validation: restore latest snapshot into a test cluster, run schema and data sanity checks, and compare to golden checksums
Wire metrics to a drill dashboard (grafana link) and emit an artifacts package (logs, traces, outcomes) to the drill S3 bucket
run_notes: 2026-02-19 - Liam Patel: Spike to prototype runner; initial script can simulate region blackhole by dropping connections at the LB layer
2026-02-25 - Ava Chen: Implemented circuit-breaker trip/untrip via admin endpoint; observed recovery flapping at 10s intervals under current policy
2026-03-02 - Reliability review (Ava, Samira, Mateo): Decided to increase circuit breaker closed->open threshold from 30% to 45% error rate for services with >200 RPS to reduce alert noise
2026-03-05 - PM feedback (Noah): Add a lightweight canary phase before full failover in runbook to protect high-value customers
2026-03-08 - Engineering: Backup restore script added; found an edge-case migration that drops new enum values — added schema check to acceptance criteria
decisions: Keep active-passive model for critical customer namespaces but add a configurable slow-roll cutover in the runbook
Circuit breaker tuning: use latency-weighted error rate, not simple 5xx count, for trip decision in high-tail services
Load-shedding tiers: introduce two priority buckets (gold/standard) with explicit L4 drops for standard under high memory pressure
risks: Simulations may not capture complex cross-region dependency patterns (eg. shared caches) — false sense of security
Backup restores in staging may not reflect production scale timing; include a margin in timing SLOs
Circuit breaker misconfiguration could cause premature failovers during noisy neighbor events
post_mortem_template: Summary of drill objective and audience
Timeline of events with timestamps and actor (script, operator)
SLO impacts (latency, error budget used) and root causes
Action items with owners and due dates
